task_title: fix: type inference with auxiliary hook handlers
problem_statement:
Title: Auxiliary hook handlers should not override schema inference

Current Behavior:
When a route uses a custom type provider and an auxiliary hook handler is assigned to a variable, TypeScript infers the route schema from the hook signature instead of from the `schema` option. As a result, request properties such as `req.query`, `req.body`, or `req.params` fall back to `unknown` inside the route handler even though the schema and type provider should determine a more specific type. The regression shows up with shorthand routes like `fastify.get()` and also with `fastify.route({ ... })`.

Expected Behavior:
Schema inference should continue to come from the `schema` option even when `onRequest`, `preHandler`, or other auxiliary hooks are supplied via variables or hook arrays. With a custom type provider, the route handler should see the provider-derived types for `req.query`, `req.body`, and `req.params` in both shorthand routes and `fastify.route({ ... })` declarations.

Context:
The affected type definitions live in `types/route.d.ts`, especially `RouteShorthandOptions`, `RouteShorthandOptionsWithHandler`, and `RouteOptions`. Hook option types such as `onRequest` and `preHandler`, plus the route `handler`, all reference the `SchemaCompiler` generic that TypeScript is inferring too aggressively.

Constraints:
Do not change Fastify runtime behavior or public APIs. Keep the existing hook signatures and route handler shapes intact. The fix should stay in the type definitions and should not modify `.helix/Dockerfile.helix` or `.helix/run-tests-eval.sh`.

Edge Cases:
Handle auxiliary hook handlers that are stored in variables, hook arrays like `preHandler: [auxiliaryHandler]`, and the object-style `fastify.route({ ... })` API. The request types should stay specific for multiple schema keys such as `querystring`, `body`, and `params`.
hints: Inspect `RouteShorthandOptions`, `RouteShorthandOptionsWithHandler`, and `RouteOptions` in `types/route.d.ts`. The `SchemaCompiler` generic is currently being inferred from auxiliary hook handler variables as well as from the route schema. TypeScript 5.4+ provides `NoInfer<T>` for freezing a generic parameter so the schema stays the inference source while hooks and handlers still receive the resolved types.
